explanation: The log entry reads 'First actual case of bug being found', a joke, because engineers had called faults bugs for decades. Thomas Edison used the word in the 1870s.

claims.text: In 1947 engineers working on the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth in a relay and taped it into the logbook.
The insect taped into the Mark II logbook was not a cockroach, a beetle or a fly.
The logbook entry beside the moth reads 'First actual case of bug being found'.
Engineers had used 'bug' to mean a technical fault for decades before 1947.
Thomas Edison used the word bug for technical faults in the 1870s.
